title: The Shadow

full_text:
In the hot southern lands, a learned scholar sat upon his balcony on a warm evening. Opposite his lodging stood a mysterious house where radiant flowers bloomed and enchanting music echoed through the night. The scholar humorously told his shadow: "Go across the street and see what is inside!"

The shadow obeyed: it detached itself from the scholar's feet, crossed the street, and disappeared through the opposite doorway!

Years passed. The scholar returned to his northern homeland, writing noble books on truth, beauty, and virtue; but people cared little for his deep philosophy.

One evening, a wealthy, haughty gentleman knocked at his study door. It was his former shadow! Dressed in fine clothes, adorned with diamonds and gold chains, the shadow had learned all the shameful secrets and private vices of humanity, becoming immensely wealthy through blackmail and flattery.

"I have become a master of the world," boasted the shadow. "You, my dear scholar, are poor and neglected. Travel with me as my companion; you shall have fine food, but you must pretend that you are my shadow!"

The noble scholar refused to live a lie. But the shadow had won the favor of a foreign princess who suffered from the disease of seeing too clearly. The cunning shadow persuaded the princess to marry him, and denounced the honest scholar as a madman who claimed to be his master!

On the night of the royal wedding, while bells rang and wine flowed in the palace, the honest scholar was quietly executed in the prison dungeon. And the triumphant shadow reigned over the empire—a chilling warning of what happens when superficial illusion conquers substance and truth.
moral: When superficial appearances and cynical cunning usurp the place of truth and intellect, humanity falls into servitude.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Shadow"?
options: Andersen's tales teach compassion, resilience, and Christian hope
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
